title: A short caption stays a pill instead of collapsing into a pointed oval
goal: An arrow caption with very little in it draws as a pointed oval, two arcs meeting at a point on each side, because the rounded ends are wider than the pill itself. A caption should always read as a pill or a badge: never narrower than its own height plus a margin, and never able to form a point.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-05 with a screenshot of a nearly empty caption drawn as a lens. Cause found by reading: PillRasterizer line 54 takes the corner radius as chipSize.height / 2 unconditionally and builds a rounded rect with it. When the width is less than the height the two rounded ends overlap and the path degenerates into two arcs meeting at points, which is exactly the shape in the screenshot. Two changes, both needed: clamp the radius to half the SMALLER side so the path can never degenerate, and give the pill a minimum width of its height times about 1.2 so a short label still reads as a pill rather than a circle. The size comes from AnnotationContent.estimatedCaptionSize (Layer.swift line 262), which is a generous estimate used for frame reservation, while the rasterizer measures the real text and draws a smaller pill from the same attachment; apply the minimum in BOTH so the reserved box still contains what is drawn. Note the related task an-arrow-can-wear-a-different-head-and-its-pill makes the corner radius adjustable; the clamp has to hold for every radius that task allows, so whichever lands second should keep the other rule.
acceptance: A caption pill is never narrower than its height plus about a fifth, however short the text is, including an empty one
No caption ever draws with a point on its side, at any font size, stroke width or zoom
A caption with plenty of text is exactly the size it is today
The text stays centred in the wider pill
Pixel tests in PhotonzRender cover an empty caption, a one character caption and a long one, written before the change
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a one character and an empty caption beside a normal one, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Epic check: epic-uehjr1 is staged later, but it is later because it FINISHED, its parent measure-redline is now, and this is a defect the user reported with a screenshot against shipped Next work. Fixed rather than dropped.

Adversarial review before building. Reproduced first by rendering every caption length through the real rasterizer. Finding: the pointed oval in the report is already gone, fixed hours later the same day by 9903141, which clamped the corner radius to half the SHORT side. What remains is the tall narrow lozenge: at 20pt the pill is 45.8 tall, and captions up to two characters measure 27-41 wide. So the shortest version that delivers the value is the minimum-width rule alone, plus a regression test pinning the clamp so the adjustable-corner-radius task cannot bring the point back.

Second finding: the floor has to be a number BOTH the rasterizer (which measures real glyphs) and estimatedCaptionSize (which counts characters) can compute identically, or the reserved frame is narrower than the drawn pill and clips it. Made it captionMinPillWidth, derived from font size and padding alone: (captionFontSize * 1.4 + 2 * padding) * 1.2, where 1.4 is SF Pro's line height and matches the measured text height to within a hundredth of a point.
Third finding: the caption FIELD did not need widening. An empty field is already sized by its 'Caption, Esc to skip' hint, confirmed in a real capture.

Tests written first, watched fail: Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/CaptionPillShapeTests.swift (6 pixel tests over empty, one character and long captions at 10/20/48pt) and 5 model tests in AnnotationCaptionTests. Then the change: captionMinPillWidth on AnnotationContent, applied in captionPillSize(forTextSize:) and estimatedCaptionSize. Full suite green, 3414 tests.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the real app: Scripts/playtest/short-caption-pill-walk.json on the probe build, three arrows captioned 1, Hi and Primary action. Screen Recording granted, so real window captures. The short pills read as badges lying on their side and the long one is untouched. Honest note: a one character pill still reads as a fat rounded badge rather than a stadium at the fifth the task asked for. Kept the stated rule and raised it in the audit rather than inventing a wider one.

Two follow-ups filed instead of scope creep: a-one-or-two-digit-measurement-stays-a-pill-inst (a caliper reading 4 is 32x42, the same defect on the measure chip, but widening it moves geometry that the chip-join and callout-clearance suites assert against) and words-sit-in-the-middle-of-their-pill-not-two-po (text sits 2.5px left of centre in every pill, pre-existing, measured identical on widened and natural pills).
